guidelines.detail: refines ACT-05 (The generator modeled the outside participants' building work as an intermediate catch event labeled with its completion ('House built', X7). The reference models that work as a manual task (M5). The description names the work as something the process requested and then continues after, with no message, timer or condition described as the awaited occurrence. So the difference comes from the choice)

same as LRN-075 (Four generated task labels (P2, P4, P5, P3) add a recipient or qualifying phrase, or restate the object, relative to the description's verb-object wording, and this drives the semantic divergence from the reference labels. LRN-075 already asks for the description's own verb and object without added recipients or circumstances, with those moved to events, gateway branches or flows. The proposed gui)

refines COL-04 (The reference models the architect and the online stores as separate pools, with message flows for sending requirements and orders and for returning the draft and the goods. The generated model has none of these pools or flows. Each outside party performs work after receiving the request (drafting, processing the order), so it is not a mere offer-giver and LRN-046 does not apply. LRN-053 covers on)

new guideline (The generated model uses a sendTask for the ordering step (X2), while the reference has a userTask for placing the order (M1). The description says the person orders the materials from several online stores (S5), which is work the person performs, not a message to another party. The closest learned guideline LRN-059 gives a user task only when the description names a software system, and the descr)

same as LRN-091 (The reference has pools for the architect and the online stores, message flows from the sending tasks to those pools, and message flows from those pools to the catch events 'draft received' and 'Get order'. The generated model has none of these. The description states that the outside parties do not perform the rest of the process and that the participant waits for their returned items. This match)

The ordering step described in S5 is missing from the generated model after the list task, so it is an omitted action rather than a labeling error. The label pairs mostly follow the description: P2 and P3 match S6 and S4, and P1 adds a decision the description does not state, so the reference is the side that diverges there. The closest learned guideline, LRN-0)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant outside the process is asked to carry out a piece of work, and a later step is described as following the completion of that work, with no message, signal, timer or condition named as the thing the process waits for: Model the requested work as a task (a manual task when it is done without a system) placed in the sequence where the description places it, after the step that requests it. Model the request itself as a send step, and use an intermediate catch event only for an explicitly described message, signal, timer or condition. Do not replace the performed work with a catch event that names its completion.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant outside the process is asked to carry out a piece of work, and a later step is described as following the completion of that work, with no message, signal, timer or condition named as the thing the process waits for

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names a work activity with its own verb and object, and a generated task label would use a different verb, a synonym, a restated object, or extra words such as a recipient, a reaction, or a circumstance that the description does not attach to that activity's own action: Label the task with the verb and object words that the description uses for that activity, in the same order and without synonyms or added qualifiers. Model any circumstance, reaction, or recipient that the description states separately as an event, a gateway branch, or the sequence flow leading to the task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a work activity with its own verb and object, and a generated task label would append a recipient, a qualifying phrase, or a restated object that the description attaches to a different step or does not attach to the activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a participant sends a request or order to one or more outside participants that do not perform the rest of the process, and one or more of those outside participants later send an item back that the participant waits for before continuing: Model each outside participant as its own bpmn:participant pool in the collaboration. Place the sending task in the requesting participant's pool and draw a message flow from that task to the outside pool. Model each wait for a returned item as an intermediate catch event in the requesting participant's pool, and draw a message flow from the outside pool to that catch event, so that the direction of every message matches the description. When the description says the participant continues only after several such items have arrived, join the waiting branches with a parallel gateway before the next step.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a participant sends a request or order to one or more outside participants that do not perform the rest of the process, and one or more of those outside participants later send an item back that the participant waits for before continuing

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an actor, after deriving a list of items from a plan, places a manual purchase of those items with one or more external vendors, and then describes other actions as running while that purchase is pending: Model the manual purchase as a user task in the actor's lane. Place it directly after the task that creates the item list and before the parallel gateway that starts the concurrent actions. Connect the list task to the purchase task, and connect the purchase task to that parallel gateway. Do not model a manual purchase as a send task, and do not connect the list task directly to the parallel gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an actor, after deriving a list of items from a plan, places a manual purchase of those items with one or more external vendors, and then describes other actions as running while that purchase is pending

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a person places orders with external suppliers through a software system or web-based shop for items the person needs, and the ordering is an action the person carries out before the process continues: Model the placing of such orders as a user task (userTask) in the lane of the person who performs them, placed in the sequence where the description places the ordering. Do not model that ordering action as a send task, because a send task is reserved for cases where sending a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a person places orders with external suppliers through a software system or web-based shop for items the person needs, and the ordering is an action the person carries out before the process continues
